table.name: ordo_reorder_cycle
table.comment: Detected reorder cycle per customer and SKU

column.name: avg_interval_days
column.comment: Average interval between orders, in days

column.name: last_order_date
column.comment: Date of the most recent order containing this SKU

column.name: next_expected_date
column.comment: Predicted date of the next order

column.name: orders_considered
column.comment: Number of past orders used to compute the cycle

table.name: ordo_reorder_reminder_log
table.comment: Log of sent reorder reminders, to avoid duplicate sends

column.name: reacted
column.comment: Whether the customer placed a matching order after the reminder

table.name: ordo_abandoned_cart_reminder_log
table.comment: Log of sent abandoned cart reminders, to cap reminders per cart

table.name: ordo_offer
table.comment: B2B offer/quote with an expiration date — the entity Magento Open Source does not have natively

column.name: extension_count
column.comment: Number of times the customer self-extended the expiry

table.name: ordo_offer_reminder_log
table.comment: Log of sent offer expiry reminders, to avoid duplicate sends

table.name: ordo_credit_limit_alert_log
table.comment: Log of sent credit limit alerts, one row per threshold band crossed, to control alert frequency

table.name: ordo_segment
table.comment: A saved, reusable set of AND-ed conditions (customer attributes/behavior) — built from the same ConditionPool campaigns use, so any condition type (tag, order total, RFM, score) works here too. Referenced by the in_segment campaign condition and reused across as many campaigns as needed, instead of re-declaring the same conditions inline in every campaign that wants them.

column.name: condition_logic
column.comment: 'all' (AND, default) or 'any' (OR) across this segment's conditions - see Model\Segment\SegmentMatcher/SegmentMemberResolver

column.name: estimated_audience_size
column.comment: Cached count of customers currently matching this segment, refreshed periodically by Cron\RecalculateSegmentAudienceSizes for the segment grid. Null means never computed yet (e.g. brand new segment) - see Model\Segment\SegmentMemberResolver for the live, on-demand equivalent used on the edit page and by BulkAction.

column.name: audience_size_computed_at
column.comment: When estimated_audience_size was last refreshed - shown next to the grid count so it reads as a snapshot, not a live number

table.name: ordo_segment_condition
table.comment: One AND-ed condition on a segment — same type/params shape as ordo_campaign_condition, evaluated through the same ConditionPool

column.name: type
column.comment: Condition type key, matches Model\Campaign\ConditionPool registration

table.name: ordo_customer_score
table.comment: Lead scoring — a running points total per customer, accumulated by the add_points campaign action and read by the score_at_least condition. One row per customer; points accumulate via UPSERT, never a separate ledger row per event.

column.name: score
column.comment: Running points total — can go negative if a rule subtracts more than the balance

table.name: ordo_customer_tag
table.comment: Behavioral tags — the segmentation primitive every B2C trigger and future campaign targeting reads from

column.name: tag
column.comment: Tag, e.g. new_customer, vip, inactive, win_back_sent

table.name: ordo_order_approval
table.comment: Approval hold for orders placed above a customer spend limit — the minimal stand-in for a B2B approval workflow

column.name: admin_email
column.comment: Email of the person who must approve

column.name: token
column.comment: Opaque token used in the approve/reject links, no login required

table.name: ordo_campaign
table.comment: A configurable when-X-happens-and-Y-is-true-do-Z marketing rule

column.name: trigger_event
column.comment: DEPRECATED — superseded by ordo_campaign_trigger (a campaign can have more than one trigger now). Kept nullable, unread by any code path, purely so Setup\Patch\Data\MigrateCampaignTriggerToChildTable has a column to read from on upgrade. Safe to drop in a follow-up schema-only release once every install has run that patch.

column.name: condition_logic
column.comment: 'all' (AND, default) or 'any' (OR) across this campaign's conditions - see CampaignDispatcher::allConditionsSatisfied()

table.name: ordo_campaign_trigger
table.comment: One trigger event that starts a campaign — a campaign can fire on more than one, e.g. both customer_registered and tag_added, running the same conditions/actions either way

column.name: trigger_event
column.comment: e.g. order_placed, customer_registered, tag_added, scheduled_at, recurring_schedule

column.name: params
column.comment: JSON-encoded trigger configuration for the scheduled_at and recurring_schedule trigger types. Unused and null for every event-based trigger type, which carries no config of its own - see CampaignTrigger getParams method.

table.name: ordo_campaign_condition
table.comment: One AND-ed condition on a campaign

column.name: type
column.comment: Condition type key, matches Model\Campaign\ConditionPool registration

table.name: ordo_campaign_action
table.comment: One action a campaign runs, in sort_order, once all its conditions pass

column.name: type
column.comment: Action type key, matches Model\Campaign\ActionPool registration

column.name: delay_minutes
column.comment: Minutes to wait after the previous action (or the trigger, if this is the first) before running this one. 0 runs immediately, in the same dispatch as everything before it.

table.name: ordo_campaign_scheduled_action
table.comment: A paused campaign action chain waiting on a delay_minutes step — CampaignDispatcher stops running its actions synchronously the moment it reaches one with a delay and writes one of these instead of blocking. Cron\RunScheduledCampaignActions resumes the chain (starting at, and including, resume_action_id) once run_at has passed.

column.name: resume_action_id
column.comment: ordo_campaign_action.entity_id — the delayed action to run when this row is resumed, then continue on to the rest of the chain

column.name: context
column.comment: JSON-encoded dispatch context (customer_id, order_id, etc. — whatever the trigger observer originally passed in, including any mutations earlier, non-delayed actions in the same chain made before the delay was hit)

column.name: run_at
column.comment: Earliest time this row is eligible to resume

column.name: executed_at
column.comment: Set the moment the cron claims this row, before running it — not just on success — so a row can never be picked up twice even if execution itself throws

table.name: ordo_campaign_scheduled_trigger_state
table.comment: Fire-tracking for scheduled_at/recurring_schedule campaign triggers, kept separate from ordo_campaign_trigger itself: CampaignSaveProcessor deletes and recreates every trigger row on every campaign save (see its own saveTriggers() comment), which would silently wipe fire-tracking on an unrelated re-save (e.g. renaming the campaign) if it lived on that row instead. config_hash guards the other direction: an actual change to the scheduled date/cron expression changes the hash too, so Model\Campaign\ScheduledTriggerScanner treats it as a fresh, not-yet-fired config rather than something already fired under the old value.

column.name: config_hash
column.comment: sha256 of the trigger row's params JSON at the time it last fired (or was last checked)

column.name: last_fired_at
column.comment: Null until this exact config has fired at least once. recurring_schedule also uses this to avoid re-firing within the same matching minute if the scan cron runs more than once per minute.

table.name: ordo_visitor_event
table.comment: Raw on-site behavior events — short-lived by design, see PruneVisitorEvents. Deliberately kept separate from ordo_campaign/ordo_customer_tag, which are low-frequency and long-lived.

column.name: customer_id
column.comment: Set once identity stitching links this visitor to a logged-in customer

column.name: event_key
column.comment: e.g. the SKU or category id the event was about, for grouping

table.name: ordo_visitor_tag
table.comment: Behavioral tags for anonymous, never-logged-in visitors — the same segmentation primitive as ordo_customer_tag, keyed by visitor_id instead of customer_id since an anonymous visitor has no customer row to attach to yet

column.name: visitor_id
column.comment: Anonymous first-party cookie value, matches ordo_visitor_event.visitor_id

table.name: ordo_pending_popup
table.comment: A popup/banner a campaign popup action queued for a visitor or customer to see on their next poll — claimed (delivered_at set) the moment Controller\Track\Popup hands it out, the same claim-before-use pattern as ordo_campaign_scheduled_action, so a slow/duplicate poll can never deliver the same popup twice.

column.name: customer_id
column.comment: Set when the campaign context that produced this popup had a logged-in customer

column.name: visitor_id
column.comment: Set when the campaign context that produced this popup had an anonymous visitor_id — at least one of customer_id/visitor_id is always set

column.name: delivered_at
column.comment: Set the moment Controller\Track\Popup claims and hands this row out — not before, or a slow concurrent poll could double-deliver

column.name: expires_at
column.comment: If never polled by this time, PrunePendingPopups deletes it as stale rather than delivering something no longer relevant

table.name: ordo_notification
table.comment: A persistent, non-modal in-site notification a campaign notify action queued for a visitor or customer — unlike ordo_pending_popup, this is NEVER claimed-and-gone: Controller\Track\Notification returns every unread, unexpired row on EVERY poll, so it survives a page reload and keeps showing until the visitor explicitly dismisses it (Controller\Track\DismissNotification sets read_at) or it expires.

column.name: customer_id
column.comment: Set when the campaign context that produced this notification had a logged-in customer

column.name: visitor_id
column.comment: Set when the campaign context that produced this notification had an anonymous visitor_id — at least one of customer_id/visitor_id is always set

column.name: read_at
column.comment: Set only when the visitor/customer explicitly dismisses this notification - never set automatically on delivery, unlike ordo_pending_popup.delivered_at

column.name: expires_at
column.comment: If never read by this time, Cron\PruneNotifications deletes it as stale rather than continuing to show something no longer relevant

table.name: ordo_survey_prompt
table.comment: A single-question 0-10 satisfaction/NPS prompt a campaign nps_survey action queued for a visitor or customer — one row is both the queued prompt and its eventual response: claimed (delivered_at set) the moment Controller\Track\Survey hands it out, same claim-before-use pattern as ordo_pending_popup, then optionally answered once (score/responded_at set) by Controller\Track\SubmitSurveyResponse. Model\Campaign\Condition\NpsScoreAtLeast reads the most recent responded row per customer.

column.name: customer_id
column.comment: Set when the campaign context that produced this prompt had a logged-in customer

column.name: visitor_id
column.comment: Set when the campaign context that produced this prompt had an anonymous visitor_id — at least one of customer_id/visitor_id is always set

column.name: question
column.comment: The single question asked, e.g. How likely are you to recommend us to a friend?

column.name: delivered_at
column.comment: Set the moment Controller\Track\Survey claims and hands this row out — not before, or a slow concurrent poll could double-deliver

column.name: score
column.comment: The 0-10 response — nullable until answered, and never overwritten once set

column.name: responded_at
column.comment: Set only when the visitor/customer submits a score — never set automatically on delivery

column.name: expires_at
column.comment: If never polled by this time, Cron\PruneSurveyPrompts deletes it as stale rather than delivering something no longer relevant

table.name: ordo_customer_consent
table.comment: Per-customer, per-channel marketing consent state - the source of truth Model\ConsentManager reads before send_email/send_sms actually send anything. One row per customer_id+channel pair (see the unique constraint below); a customer with no row for a channel is treated as consented by default (opt-out register, not opt-in) - see the ConsentManager class doc for why.

column.name: customer_id
column.comment: The customer this consent state applies to

column.name: source
column.comment: Where this state was recorded from, e.g. admin, unsubscribe_link, checkout

table.name: ordo_ad_audience
table.comment: A segment configured to sync as a remarketing audience to an external ad platform (google_ads or meta) - Cron\SyncAdAudiences hashes each matching segment members email (Model\AdAudience\PiiHasher) and pushes the list via the platform SyncClientInterface implementation, refreshed on a cron.

column.name: segment_id
column.comment: The segment whose current members are synced

column.name: external_audience_id
column.comment: The platform side audience/customer-match-list id this syncs into - blank until the first successful sync creates or is told one

column.name: last_synced_at
column.comment: Set on every sync attempt, success or failure

column.name: last_sync_message
column.comment: Error detail, or a short success summary (e.g. row count synced)

table.name: ordo_free_gift_offer
table.comment: Free-gift-above-threshold offer header

table.name: ordo_free_gift_offer_tier
table.comment: Cascading cart-subtotal thresholds for a free-gift offer — every tier the cart subtotal has reached ADDS gift_slots, cumulative, not highest-tier-wins

column.name: min_subtotal
column.comment: Cart subtotal this tier requires to unlock its gift_slots

column.name: gift_slots
column.comment: Gift slots this tier adds once its min_subtotal is met

table.name: ordo_free_gift_offer_product
table.comment: Pool of SKUs a customer may pick a free gift from, for a given offer

table.name: ordo_trigger_outcome_log
table.comment: Sent/response stats for the 5 cron-driven triggers (reorder reminder, offer expiry, credit limit alert, order approval, win-back) — additive to each trigger's own narrow dedup log table, purely for dashboard observability

column.name: sent_at
column.comment: When the trigger email was sent

column.name: acted_at
column.comment: Set once the customer places an order after being sent this trigger — null until/unless they respond

column.name: order_id
column.comment: sales_order.entity_id — the order that constitutes the response, set together with acted_at

table.name: ordo_quote_gift_item
table.comment: Marks a quote_item as a customer-selected free gift, so it can be identified/removed without guessing from price alone

column.name: offer_id
column.comment: ordo_free_gift_offer.entity_id this gift was earned from

table.name: ordo_score_rule
table.comment: Declarative demographic-attribute lead scoring rule — if a customer's attribute value matches, points are awarded (or subtracted) toward their lead score

column.name: attribute_code
column.comment: Customer attribute code, e.g. group_id, website_id, email, store_id, or any EAV custom attribute code

column.name: value
column.comment: Value to compare the attribute against

column.name: points
column.comment: Points awarded when this rule matches — can be negative

table.name: ordo_customer_demographic_score
table.comment: Current sum of matching ordo_score_rule points per customer, tracked separately from ordo_customer_score so a rule change's delta can be computed and applied additively instead of re-summing every rule on every save

column.name: score
column.comment: Current sum of matching demographic scoring rule points

table.name: ordo_customer_rfm_score
table.comment: Precomputed RFM percentile ranks and 1-5 quintile buckets per customer, refreshed by Cron\RecomputeRfmScores instead of RfmCalculator::getPercentileRanks() scanning/sorting the whole customer base on every campaign dispatch or segment resolve

column.name: computed_at
column.comment: When Cron\RecomputeRfmScores last wrote this row

table.name: ordo_content_block
table.comment: A reusable, admin-authored piece of email content — static HTML snippet, RSS-newsletter feed, or product listing feed — resolvable by a campaign's add_dynamic_content action so the same block can be reused across many campaigns

column.name: type
column.comment: Content producer type: snippet, rss, product_feed — matches Model\ContentBlock\ProducerPool registration

column.name: config
column.comment: JSON-encoded type-specific config: snippet {html}; rss {feed_url, item_count}; product_feed {source: category|rule, category_id, rule_id, item_count}

column.name: enabled
column.comment: Whether this block can currently be resolved by a campaign action

table.name: ordo_content_block_rss_cache
table.comment: Last successfully fetched+rendered HTML for an RSS-type content block, refreshed every 30 min by Cron\RefreshRssContentBlocks — dispatch-time reads never hit the network

column.name: rendered_html
column.comment: Cached inline-styled HTML fragment ready to embed in an email

column.name: fetched_at
column.comment: When this feed was last successfully fetched and rendered

column.name: fetch_error
column.comment: Last fetch error message, kept for admin diagnostics even though stale rendered_html is still served

table.name: ordo_product_feed_cache
table.comment: Last successfully generated shopping feed XML, refreshed by Cron\RefreshProductFeed - Controller\ProductFeed\Index serves this cached row on every public request, never generating on demand. One row per feed_code (only google_merchant today, kept per-code rather than a singleton row so a second feed format can be added without a schema change).

column.name: product_count
column.comment: How many items the last successful generation produced

column.name: generated_at
column.comment: When this feed was last successfully generated

column.name: generation_error
column.comment: Last generation error message, kept for admin diagnostics even though stale xml is still served

table.name: ordo_message_log
table.comment: One row per individual outbound message a campaign action dispatched — deliberately channel-generic so sms/email/whatsapp all share the same table/webhook shape instead of a one-off design per channel

column.name: channel
column.comment: Delivery channel: sms, email, or whatsapp

column.name: to_address
column.comment: Phone number or email address the message was sent to

column.name: provider_message_id
column.comment: The provider's own message ID (Twilio's Sid) — what a delivery-status webhook looks this row up by

column.name: status
column.comment: sent, delivered, failed, undelivered, opted_out, or suppressed - opted_out is distinct from failed (see Model/Sms/OptedOutException), suppressed means the cross-channel frequency cap blocked this send before it was ever attempted (see Model/Campaign/FrequencyCapManager)

column.name: error_code
column.comment: Provider error code, if the status is failed/undelivered/opted_out

column.name: sent_at
column.comment: When this module attempted the send

column.name: updated_at
column.comment: Last time a delivery-status callback updated this row

column.name: campaign_id
column.comment: ordo_campaign.entity_id that triggered this send, if any — null for a non-campaign-driven send (e.g. a direct admin test send). No FK: a historical log row must survive the campaign it came from being deleted, same reasoning customer_id already has no FK here.

column.name: variant
column.comment: Split-test variant key (see a campaign action's own 'split' type) this send belongs to, if the sending action was inside a split. Null for a non-split-tested send.

table.name: ordo_message_log_event
table.comment: One row per open/click event a delivery-status webhook reported for a given ordo_message_log row — a separate event log rather than another ordo_message_log.status value, since a single message can be opened/clicked more than once and funnel counting needs each stage counted independently rather than collapsed into one terminal status

column.name: url
column.comment: The clicked URL, for a clicked event — null for opened

table.name: ordo_campaign_outcome_log
table.comment: Sent/converted stats per campaign (and split-test variant) — the campaign-scoped counterpart of ordo_trigger_outcome_log, same first-plausible-match attribution philosophy (Observer\RecordCampaignOutcome sets acted_at/order_id once the customer places an order, not exact/billing-grade attribution). Additive to ordo_message_log, which already records the send itself; this table exists purely to answer 'did this campaign convert.'

column.name: variant
column.comment: Split-test variant key, if this send was inside a split action — null otherwise

column.name: acted_at
column.comment: Set once the customer places an order after this send — null until/unless they respond

column.name: order_id
column.comment: sales_order.entity_id — the order that constitutes the conversion, set together with acted_at

table.name: ordo_whatsapp_template
table.comment: A WhatsApp message template - the WhatsApp Business Platform only allows sending a free-form message inside a 24-hour customer-service window; anything outside that window (which is most campaign sends) must use a pre-approved template registered with Meta via Model/WhatsApp/WhatsAppTemplateClient, tracked here through its own approval lifecycle before the send_whatsapp campaign action is allowed to use it

column.name: meta_template_name
column.comment: The name registered with Meta - lowercase letters/digits/underscores only, distinct from the admin-facing name above

column.name: category
column.comment: marketing, utility, or authentication - see Model/Config/Source/WhatsAppTemplateCategory, drives Meta's own approval rules and per-message pricing

column.name: language
column.comment: Meta locale code, e.g. en_US, pl_PL

column.name: body_text
column.comment: The template body Meta approves - {{1}}, {{2}}, ... placeholders filled positionally by the send_whatsapp campaign action's own params at send time

column.name: meta_template_id
column.comment: Meta's own template id, set once SubmitForReview succeeds - what RefreshStatus polls by

column.name: status
column.comment: draft, pending, approved, rejected, or disabled - see Model/WhatsAppTemplate::STATUS_* - only approved templates can be used by send_whatsapp

column.name: rejection_reason
column.comment: Meta's own rejection reason, if status is rejected

column.name: submitted_at
column.comment: When SubmitForReview last sent this to Meta

table.name: ordo_push_subscription
table.comment: A single browser/device's Web Push subscription (RFC 8030/8291) - one row per endpoint, since a customer commonly has more than one (phone + laptop). Keyed by customer_id OR visitor_id, same anonymous-then-stitched shape as ordo_visitor_tag/ordo_pending_popup - a visitor can grant notification permission before ever logging in.

column.name: customer_id
column.comment: Set once identity stitching links this subscription's visitor_id to a logged-in customer, or immediately if the browser was already logged in when it subscribed

column.name: visitor_id
column.comment: Anonymous first-party cookie value, matches ordo_visitor_event.visitor_id - at least one of customer_id/visitor_id is always set

column.name: endpoint
column.comment: The push service URL (fcm.googleapis.com/..., updates.push.services.mozilla.com/..., etc.) PushSender posts the encrypted message to - can exceed 255 chars for some browsers, hence text not varchar

column.name: endpoint_hash
column.comment: sha256(endpoint) - endpoint itself is a text column and can't be usefully unique-indexed/looked-up directly in InnoDB, this is what PushSubscriptionManager actually queries/uniques on

column.name: p256dh_key
column.comment: Subscription's P-256 ECDH public key (base64url), from PushSubscription.getKey('p256dh') in the browser - PushSender's own ephemeral key is combined with this to derive the message encryption key, see RFC 8291

column.name: auth_key
column.comment: Subscription's 16-byte auth secret (base64url), from PushSubscription.getKey('auth') - the other HKDF input RFC 8291 requires alongside p256dh_key

column.name: last_seen_at
column.comment: Last time this endpoint was (re)registered - browsers can rotate the endpoint/keys of an existing subscription without an explicit unsubscribe, so a fresh register just updates this row rather than creating a duplicate
